items.prompt: Black to move. Find the move the engine ranks first.

claims.statement: 17...b4 is legal.
In a multi-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is b4.
A white knight stands on c3.
A black pawn stands on b5.
After b4, exactly one black piece attacks c3: the pawn.
g6 is at least 80 centipawns below the top move at depth 16.

hints: Look at White's knight on c3 and ask what guards it and where it can go.
A pawn move can ask a piece a question and take space at the same time.
Which pawn can attack the knight that has no good squares?
items.explain: At depth 16 the engine puts 17...b4 first. The pawn attacks the knight on c3 and gains space on the queenside. That is evidence for the game move, not proof that it is the only good one; the engine rates two other moves within about 0.4 pawn.

feedback_by_move.g7g6: At depth 16 the engine rates g6 at least 80 centipawns below b4.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 20...fxe4 is legal.
In a multi-line search at depth 16 the engine's first choice is fxe4.
A black knight stands on h5.
Before the move one white piece attacks h5: the queen on d1.
Before the move the knight on h5 is loose (attacked, and defended by nothing).
After fxe4 the knight on h5 is still loose.
Nxg3 is at least 150 centipawns below the top move at depth 16.

hints: Check which of your pieces is already attacked and whether anything defends it.
You cannot save everything, so ask what the best use of this move is.
The f-pawn takes on e4; the knight on h5 can then be taken, but the rook on f8 has a target on f2.
items.explain: At depth 16 the engine puts 20...fxe4 clearly first, well ahead of the next move. The knight on h5 was already attacked by the queen and defended by nothing; after fxe4 the queen can take it, and the game continued 21.Qxh5 Rxf2. A piece is given up here on purpose, so compare the positions after each capture before you decide.

feedback_by_move.h5g3: At depth 16 the engine rates Nxg3 at least 150 centipawns below fxe4.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 23...R8f5 is legal.
23...h6 is legal.
At depth 16 the engine's first choice is R8f5 and h6 is within 40 centipawns of it.
The white queen stands on g5.
A black rook stands on f2.

hints: Look at White's queen: how many safe squares does it have, and which of your pieces can take some away?
A rook lift can attack the queen and keep your other rook where it is.
The rook on f8 can go to f5, attacking the queen on g5.
items.explain: At depth 16 the engine puts 23...R8f5 first and rates the quiet 23...h6 within 40 centipawns, so both are accepted. R8f5 attacks the queen on g5, which has to leave. That is evidence at one depth, not proof.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 25...h6 (the game move) is legal.
25...a5 is legal.
25...h5 is legal.
At depth 16 the engine's first choice is a5, with h5 and h6 within 40 centipawns.
Qb7 is at least 90 centipawns below the top move at depth 16.

hints: White's pieces have few useful moves. Which of yours could make a move that changes nothing important?
Look for a pawn move that does not weaken anything you need.
Each of a5, h5 and h6 is a pawn move that leaves your pieces where they are.
items.explain: At depth 16 the engine's top three moves are all quiet pawn moves: a5, h5 and h6 (the game move). The engine does not single out 25...h6. What the three share is that no piece moves, and White has to find a move next. Whether that is a true zugzwang is tested in the next steps.

feedback_by_move.d7b7: At depth 16 the engine rates Qb7 at least 90 centipawns below the pawn moves.
